title: Meta Ads and Shopify Sales Don't Match? Why and How to Fix It
seoTitle: Meta Ads vs Shopify Sales Don't Match? Why and How to Fix
excerpt: Meta ads and Shopify sales don't match? Attribution windows, view-through, CAPI duplicates and COD/RTO explained, plus how to reconcile with MER.
imageAlt: A magnifying glass resting on a page of handwritten ledger figures

inlineImages.alt: A black alarm clock on a desk beside a laptop and a pen holder
inlineImages.caption: If your ad account and store use different time zones, daily numbers will never line up.

inlineImages.alt: A parcel wrapped in brown paper and tied with blue string on a white background

faqs.question: Why don't my Meta ads and Shopify sales match?
faqs.answer: They count different things. Meta credits a purchase to an ad if someone clicked or saw it within the attribution window and may model some conversions. Shopify counts each real order once and credits only channels the buyer clicked. Time zones, currency, duplicate events and cancelled COD orders widen the gap.

faqs.question: What is Meta's default attribution setting?
faqs.answer: In Meta's Insights API the default option means 7-day click and 1-day view: a purchase within seven days of clicking an ad or one day of seeing it. Meta has adjusted the setting since, including a 1-day engage-through window in 2026, so check the attribution setting on each ad set.

faqs.question: Why does Meta show more purchases than Shopify?
faqs.answer: Usually because of view-through credit, purchases also credited to Google or email, and modelled conversions. If Meta's 1-day click purchases are higher than your store's total orders, the cause is more likely duplicate events from the Pixel and Conversions API or a second app sending the same purchase.

faqs.question: How do I stop the Pixel and Conversions API counting orders twice?
faqs.answer: Make sure both send the same event name and the same event ID for each order, as Meta's deduplication guide requires, and that only one browser source and one server source send purchases. On Shopify, use the Facebook and Instagram app and remove old apps, theme snippets or tags that also send purchases.

faqs.question: How does cash on delivery affect Meta ads reporting in India?
faqs.answer: Meta records a purchase when a COD order is placed, but refused or returned parcels never reach Ads Manager, so Meta's revenue and ROAS look higher than the money you collect. Report delivered revenue from Shopify, split COD from prepaid, and work out delivered ROAS by campaign.

faqs.question: Why are Meta and GA4 conversions different?
faqs.answer: GA4 only sees visits to your website and uses its own attribution model and lookback window, so it never counts view-through purchases and often credits Google search or direct visits instead. Missing UTM tags, in-app browsers, consent banners and cross-device journeys also reduce what GA4 credits to Meta.

faqs.question: How do I reconcile Meta Ads and Shopify numbers?
faqs.answer: Align time zone and currency, test that each order shows once with the right value, then compare a complete week that ended at least seven days ago. Put Meta's default, 7-day click and 1-day click results beside Shopify's orders and net sales, and track the ratio between them over time.

faqs.question: What is MER in e-commerce?
faqs.answer: MER, the marketing efficiency ratio, is total store revenue divided by total ad spend across all channels for the same period. It doesn't depend on any platform's attribution, so it can't be inflated by double counting. Use it for overall budget decisions and Ads Manager to compare ads.

faqs.question: Should I trust Meta Ads Manager or Shopify?
faqs.answer: Trust Shopify for how many orders and how much money you actually took, and Meta for comparing campaigns and ads with each other. Neither tells the full story of what caused a sale, so pair Shopify revenue with total spend as MER when deciding whether to scale.
